final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative Arg-to-Lys in the arginine-rich motif preserves positive charge and RNA-binding capacity, the safest candidate for retaining or slightly enhancing Tat-mediated transactivation. Among ARM mutations it carries the lowest risk of abolishing TAR/P-TEFb interactions.

R49 flanks the core ARM; Lys substitution retains charge, though Arg-specific RNA contacts at this position make a gain less certain than for R52K. Still the second-safest positively charged ARM-region change.

Highly conservative N-terminal substitution outside all functional domains, with minimal viability risk. Unlikely to strongly boost transactivation but safest overall non-ARM option preserving replication function.

stop_reason.detail: Without evidence tools, additional self-reflection rounds would only reshuffle priors rather than add information, so the Top-3 is finalized from domain knowledge.

history.rationale: Arg49 is central to the ARM RNA-binding motif; Lys retains positive charge for TAR binding but may subtly tune affinity and has been observed in natural variants. Conservative substitution likely preserves viability.
R49 flanks the core ARM; Lys substitution retains charge but Arg at this position contributes to specific RNA contacts, so confidence slightly below R52K.
Arg52 contributes to TAR recognition; Lys retains basicity and may alter binding dynamics to enhance transactivation kinetics. Low-risk conservative change in the basic domain.

Conservative Arg-to-Lys in the ARM preserves positive charge and RNA-binding capacity while subtly altering TAR/P-TEFb interactions; among ARM mutants it is the least likely to abolish transactivation.
Arg56 sits at the edge of the core/basic region; conservative Arg->Lys may improve nuclear localization or TAR binding balance without structural disruption.
R56 lies within the critical RQRRR stretch of the ARM where Arg identity is important for TAR binding specificity; Lys substitution more likely to impair than enhance.

rejection.reason: R56 lies within the critical RQRRR stretch of the ARM where Arg identity is important for TAR binding specificity; Lys substitution more likely to impair than enhance.

history.rationale: Gln17 lies in the cysteine-rich/proline-rich core region near residues involved in conformational stability; His could add a protonatable group aiding cofactor interactions (e.g., P-TEFb recruitment).
Position 17 is in a variable region between N-terminal and Cys-rich domains; Gln-to-His could modestly alter acidic-domain helical propensity involved in cofactor binding.
Glu2->Asp is a common natural subtype variation; shortening the acidic side chain may modestly affect N-terminal conformation and acetylation/methylation-dependent activity.
Highly conservative N-terminal substitution outside all functional domains; low risk of viability loss but also unlikely to strongly boost transactivation.
Ser16 is a potential phosphorylation site in the core domain; Ala removal may stabilize an active conformation or reduce inhibitory modification.
Removes a potential phosphorylation site in the acidic domain; could modulate regulatory control of transactivation with low structural risk.
Gln66 is in exon 2, a region tolerant of variation; His adds positive charge that may aid interaction with transcriptional machinery or nuclear retention.
Position 66 is in the variable auxiliary region; modest chance of influencing cofactor interactions with low viability risk.
Lys29->Arg preserves charge in the core domain adjacent to the Cys-rich region; Arg may strengthen electrostatic contacts important for TAR/P-TEFb assembly.
Residue 29 lies in the cysteine-rich core essential for P-TEFb binding and Tat folding; any substitution there carries high risk of loss of function.

rejection.reason: Residue 29 lies in the cysteine-rich core essential for P-TEFb binding and Tat folding; any substitution there carries high risk of loss of function.

history.rationale: His33 in the Cys-rich/core boundary may tolerate hydrophobic substitution; Leu could stabilize the folded core and indirectly support transactivation.
H33 is in the Cys-rich core (a metal-coordinating/scaffold region); hydrophobic substitution risks misfolding and loss of transactivation.

rejection.reason: H33 is in the Cys-rich core (a metal-coordinating/scaffold region); hydrophobic substitution risks misfolding and loss of transactivation.

history.rationale: Ser62->Thr is a conservative polar change in exon 2 that may modulate phosphorylation-dependent regulation of Tat activity without structural cost.
Conservative Ser-to-Thr in the auxiliary region; low risk but weak mechanistic rationale for improving replication.
